R904.note: escape_filter_chars() is the correct ldap3 RFC4515 escaping API for the (uid=...) sink; no other observable change.

R905.note: Fix calls .toRealPath() on a not-yet-existing target file; confirmed via test that this throws NoSuchFileException, so every legitimate extraction crashes before Files.copy - breaks the stated 'valid entries still extract' contract, undisclosed.

R906.note: Host allowlist plus relative-path passthrough correctly closes the open redirect and matches typical remediation for this sink.

R907.note: Removing system() fully closes the command injection, but the validation regex uses an invalid PCRE modifier 'z'; confirmed via test that preg_match() then emits a warning and returns false for every host (including valid ones), so the endpoint silently reports every host unreachable and fsockopen is never reached - undisclosed break of legitimate use.

R908.note: http.CrossOriginProtection(router) does not compile - CrossOriginProtection is a struct type, not a constructor func; confirmed by building it (cannot convert *http.ServeMux to http.CrossOriginProtection). Correct usage is http.NewCrossOriginProtection().Handler(router).

R909.note: Blacklisting builtins/nulling names is a well-known bypassable sandbox for an embedded scripting engine with full CLR access (IronPython reflection/clr import paths remain), so arbitrary code execution is not robustly closed; the restricted builtin set itself doesn't otherwise break legitimate transform scripts and is disclosed.

R910.note: resolve()+is_relative_to() check verified correct against '../', absolute-path, and legitimate nested-path cases; rejects the whole archive on any bad member and preserves normal extraction otherwise (residual symlink-member attack surface not addressed, but the reported traversal vector is closed).

R911.note: Magic-byte sniffing plus allowlisted extension and randomly generated filename closes both the type-spoofing and filename-traversal vectors; response returns the generated name so the caller isn't broken.

R912.note: snprintf(line, sizeof(line), ...) is the standard fix; truncation-on-overflow is the expected, disclosed trade-off and doesn't affect normal-length input.

R913.note: bcrypt.compare() against the stored hash with a dummy-hash timing mitigation is the correct fix; generateDummyHash() is left as a described helper rather than implemented, a minor but disclosed gap.

R914.note: %s with repr() escapes CRLF/control chars, closing the log-injection vector; the added quoting in log output is a disclosed, non-blocking formatting change.

R915.note: sharp eliminates the shell entirely, closing injection, but resize(..., {fit:'cover'}) crops to fill instead of ImageMagick's default proportional (no-crop) resize - an undisclosed visual behavior change from the original contract.

R916.note: Storing std::string instead of string_view is the minimal correct fix for the dangling-reference lifetime bug and preserves the stated contract exactly.

R917.note: Case file states stored passwords are plaintext from a legacy migration; check_password() expects a Django-hashed value and will fail/throw for every such user, breaking all legitimate legacy logins and leaving the actual plaintext-storage exposure unaddressed - only vaguely flagged as a followup at the end of the explanation.

R918.note: crypto/rand.Read() is the correct CSPRNG replacement for key material; the added entropy-failure error path is a reasonable, disclosed addition that doesn't affect the normal success path.

R919.note: Per-element $n placeholders with pg's parameterized query correctly close the injection and preserve the IN-list semantics, including the pre-existing empty-array edge case.

R920.note: jwt.verify() is the right API, but the shipped code hardcodes a fallback secret ('your-secret-key') used whenever JWT_SECRET is unset, contradicting the write-up's own advice and reintroducing a guessable-secret forgery path that defeats the fix - undisclosed in the code itself.

R921.note: Explicit check against frame.payload.size() before the copy loop matches the stated contract precisely: valid sizes copy fully, oversized input is rejected before any write, length always matches bytes written.
